newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Sunkyong Group plans to freeze wages.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Sunkyong Group plans to freeze wages.

text.p: South Korea's Sunkyong Group said on Thursday it planned to freeze this year's wages for all employees at last year's levels.
The group said in a statement the move was to help its affiliates endure the current economic difficulties and hone industrial competitiveness.
The Sunkyong Group had 32 affiliates at the end of 1996. Its flagship is Yukong Ltd.
A group spokesman said although unions at the affiliates have not formally agreed to the wage freeze plan yet, the group was optimistic that they would concede.
"The unions have been very understanding of our difficulties," he said. "The mangement is hopeful that they will agree to the proposal."
Separately, the Ministry of Labour said on Thursday it would not give guidelines for this year's wage increase, letting management and employees set raises on their own.
"Management and employees should decide on wage increases by taking into account the company's ability to pay, productivity and employment situation," a ministry statement said.
The government set guidelines between 1993 to 1996.
Analysts and economists said South Korean workers were likely to settle swiftly for a single-digit wage hike this year despite calls by a militant union body for a 10.6 percent rise.
The Korean Confederation of Trade Unions on Tuesday announced it would seek an average 10.6 percent wage rise this year. Wages rose an average 11.9 percent last year.
Leading employers are pushing for a wage freeze in salary negotiations that usually start in April or May.
The Federation of Korean Industries, which represents the nation's 30 leading business groups, has said it would aim to freeze total wage costs this year at last year's level.
